defects.lines: behavior_notes[0] and refs Ref1 (source bandwidth.c lines 24, 452-454, 471-479)
defects.before: Each thread measures its own elapsed time between its two clock reads [Ref1]. / Ref1: Lines 471 to 479: the two clock reads of a thread and its elapsed time.
defects.after: Each thread measures its own elapsed time. It reads the clock once before its first timed pass and again after each pass over its 256 MiB buffer. The elapsed time runs from the first read to the last read [Ref1]. / Ref1: Lines 471 to 479: the clock reads of a thread (`t0` before the first timed pass, `t1` after each check step) and its elapsed time `t1 - t0`. Lines 24 and 452 to 454: a check step is 1 pass when the buffer is larger than 8 MiB.
defects.evidence: bandwidth.c reads `t1 = now_s()` inside the do-while loop after every `passes_per_check` passes, and `CHECK_BYTES` (8 MiB) / 256 MiB gives 0, which line 454 sets to 1, so a thread reads the clock about 9 times per interval and not 2 times.

defects.before: Lines used: every interval line (field 4, `rep`, is a number). Lines not used: ...
defects.after: Lines used: every header line (binary, kernel, round, load, UTC time) and every interval line (field 4, `rep`, is a number). Of an interval line the script reads fields 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9. It does not read field 2 (`threads`), field 6 (`elapsed_s`) or field 10 (`per_thread_avg_GBps`). Lines not used: ...
defects.evidence: stat_k120.py line 33 keeps 5 values of the header line, and lines 37 to 41 use only p[0], p[2], p[3], p[4], p[6], p[7] and p[8]; the unit task asks for the exact rows and columns that are read.

defects.before: (no definition of per_thread_min_GBps, per_thread_max_GBps, per_thread_avg_GBps, although the notes and the annotation use all three)
defects.after: per_thread_min_GBps, per_thread_max_GBps, per_thread_avg_GBps: fields 8, 9 and 10 of an interval line. Fields 8 and 9 are the lowest and the highest rate of one thread in the interval. Field 10 is the mean of the rates of all threads. The rate of a thread is its bytes divided by its own elapsed time, divided by 1e9 [Ref1].
defects.evidence: bandwidth.c lines 588 to 603 compute `g = bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9` per thread and print its minimum, its maximum and `sum / cfg.threads`.

defects.before: ... For the kernels `read` and `asmread` this is the number of buffer passes that all 120 threads together completed in the interval.
defects.after: (same text, then) For `copy` and `asmcopy` the binary counts read plus written bytes, as the `#` comment line of each process says. So the same division gives 2 x the number of buffer passes for these two kernels.
defects.evidence: stat_k120.py prints the label `passes` for every kernel (for example 480 for asmcopy), and bandwidth.c lines 427 to 429 and 437 to 439 return `2 * cfg.bytes` for the two copy kernels.

defects.before: - Kept per interval: `p[6]` = `aggregate_GBps`, `p[7]` = `per_thread_min_GBps`, `p[8]` = `per_thread_max_GBps`.
defects.after:
- Kept per interval: `p[6]` = `aggregate_GBps`, `p[7]` = `per_thread_min_GBps`, `p[8]` = `per_thread_max_GBps`. The last two are the lowest and the highest rate of one thread in the interval. The rate of a thread is its bytes divided by its own elapsed time [Ref1].
- Not read: `p[1]` (`threads`), `p[5]` (`elapsed_s`) and `p[9]` (`per_thread_avg_GBps`).
